title: ISO 22000 — Food Safety Management, and How It Relates to HACCP
shortDescription: A full food-safety management system that BUILDS ON HACCP rather than replacing it — a distinction exams test directly.
genZNote: HACCP finds the danger points on the line; ISO 22000 makes sure the whole kitchen actually runs like it means it.

sections.heading: What ISO 22000 Is
sections.body: ISO 22000 specifies requirements for a Food Safety Management System (FSMS) for any organization in the food chain — from primary producers and processors to transporters, storage providers, retailers, and food-service/packaging companies. First published in 2005; the current edition is ISO 22000:2018. It is certifiable, and it is built on the High Level Structure shared with ISO 9001/14001/45001, making integration with other management systems easier.

sections.heading: ISO 22000 and HACCP — Not the Same Thing
bullets: HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) is a SYSTEMATIC METHOD for identifying, evaluating, and controlling food-safety hazards at specific points in a food process — it is a technique/tool, not a full management system standard, and it is NOT an ISO standard itself.

ISO 22000 is a full MANAGEMENT SYSTEM STANDARD that explicitly incorporates HACCP principles as one of its core technical components, wrapped inside a broader organizational framework (leadership commitment, planning, resource management, documented information, internal audit, management review, continual improvement).

In short: HACCP tells you WHERE the hazards are and how to control them technically; ISO 22000 tells you how the WHOLE ORGANIZATION must be run so that hazard control actually works reliably, every day, and keeps improving.

sections.heading: Key Concepts
bullets: Food chain — covers every stage from primary production (farming, fishing) through to final consumption, recognising that food safety hazards can enter at any stage.

Prerequisite Programmes (PRPs) — basic environmental and operational conditions necessary to maintain a hygienic food-chain environment (e.g. cleaning schedules, pest control, personnel hygiene) — these underpin HACCP, they don't replace it.

Critical Control Point (CCP) — a step at which control CAN be applied and is ESSENTIAL to prevent or eliminate a food-safety hazard, or reduce it to an acceptable level (the core HACCP concept, incorporated into ISO 22000).
Hazard — a biological, chemical, or physical agent in food, or the condition of food, with the potential to cause an adverse health effect.

sections.heading: Applicability
sections.body: ISO 22000 is deliberately written to apply to organizations of any size and any position in the food chain — a small farm and a multinational packaged-food manufacturer can both be certified against it, unlike some narrower, sector-specific food-safety schemes.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: ISO 22000 is a certifiable Food Safety Management System standard that incorporates HACCP principles within a broader organizational management framework, applicable anywhere in the food chain.
keyFacts: HACCP = a hazard-control METHOD/TOOL, not an ISO standard and not a full management system.
ISO 22000 = a full FSMS standard that incorporates HACCP as a technical component.
Applies across the whole food chain — from primary production to final consumption.
commonConfusion: HACCP is NOT itself an ISO standard, and it is not a full management system — it's a hazard-analysis method that ISO 22000 builds upon.
Do not treat 'ISO 22000 certified' and 'HACCP certified' as identical claims — they test different scopes (whole management system vs a specific hazard-control method).

highYieldFacts: ISO 22000 incorporates HACCP principles but is broader than HACCP — a full FSMS, not just a hazard-analysis method.
HACCP itself is not an ISO-published standard.
commonTraps: Do not state that HACCP and ISO 22000 are interchangeable or identical — HACCP is a component technique within ISO 22000's broader system.
Do not restrict ISO 22000's applicability to food manufacturers only — it applies across the entire food chain, including transport, storage, and packaging suppliers.
mustRemember: CCP = a step where control is essential to prevent/reduce a hazard — the technical core inherited from HACCP.
PRPs are the hygiene/operational baseline that HACCP and ISO 22000 both depend on.

confusedTerms.distinction: HACCP is a specific hazard-analysis and control-point METHOD, not itself an ISO standard; ISO 22000 is a full, certifiable Food Safety Management System standard that incorporates HACCP principles within it.

possibleQuestions: Is HACCP itself an ISO standard?
What does ISO 22000 incorporate as one of its core technical components?
